An optional `fallbacks` key adds an **ordered list of further backends**, each tried — in order — only when the one before it fails to produce findings (rate-limit, unreachable, persistent transport failure, auth, not-served). The first backend that returns findings wins; the chain reaches a terminal outcome only when **every** backend has failed. This keeps the L4 second-opinion gate firing through a single provider's outage instead of silently `pass+skip`ping. - **Value is a JSON-string** — a quoted JSON array of backend objects `{provider, model, host, api_key_env?, reasoning_off?, timeout?}`. (The config parser also handles native YAML lists — `faff adversarial-backends` accepts both forms — but the JSON-string form remains the canonical shape for this key; existing configs keep working unchanged.) Omit it for the single-backend behaviour (a one-element chain — unchanged). - **Each fallback is self-contained** (its own `provider`/`model`/`host` required); omitted optional keys (`api_key_env`, `reasoning_off`, `reasoning_effort`, `reasoning_extra`, `timeout`, `first_byte_timeout`) inherit the primary's — assembled **mechanically** by `faff adversarial-backends`, never hand-`JSON.parse`d by the model (see **Backend call** below). - **No silent weakening** — an all-failed chain is never more pass-like than today's single backend: a config fault (auth / not-served / unsupported / unconfigured-default-host) anywhere in a fully-failed chain surfaces `needs-human`; only a chain of purely configured-host availability failures `pass+skip`s. The chain loop + terminal precedence live deterministically in `review-call.mjs` (`runReviewChain` / `chainTerminalExit`), not in this prose. **Per-backend context-window preflight.** A chain is tried strongest-first, so a backend skipped for a predictable reason costs you your best reviewer. Declaring `context_window` makes the advance-past-a-backend decision **proactive and window-aware** rather than leaving it to a provider HTTP 400 discovered mid-chain — which would otherwise skip the strongest backend on precisely the diffs that touch large modules, the ones most worth reviewing, and say so only in one stderr line on an otherwise-green `pass`: - **Window-targeted trim of the shared prefix — once, pre-chain, targeting the PRIMARY's usable window** (`context_window × 0.9`, the safety fraction leaving room for the response and estimate error). When the whole-file prefix plus a **fixed** brief reserve overruns it, the diff-relevance context trim is re-run at progressively tighter settings until the prefix fits the byte target, and a `[note] … window-targeted trim: …` line records what happened. The target reserves a **fixed** `DEFAULT_BRIEF_RESERVE_TOKENS` allowance rather than the actual per-lens `--system` brief, so the trimmed prefix stays a pure function of `(context, diff, primary window)` and **byte-identical across the four spec-review lenses**, which is what keeps the shared prefix cacheable across a fan-out. The trim never drops a diff-touched line, so it never degrades to the diff-only view that produced confident false criticals. - **Deterministic over-window advance.** Before dispatching *any* chain element, if that element declares a window the estimated payload does not fit, it is advanced past with `[chain] … over-window (est N tok > M usable window) → advancing (exit 2)` and **no network call is made**. The guard only ever decides a skip — it never re-trims and never alters the shared prefix, so a per-lens skip decision can differ while the prefix cannot. - **Loud surfacing, always on.** Whenever the backend that served was **not** the primary — for *any* reason (over-window guard, 400, auth, empty, deadline) — `review-call.mjs` writes the `PRIMARY_SKIP_SIGNAL` sentinel on its own stderr line and a `NOTE: primary reviewer

was skipped; served by chain[] — .` line into the findings on stdout, after the attribution header. `fan-out.mjs` recognises the sentinel by **line-anchored equality** (exactly as it does `TRUNCATION_SIGNAL`, so review content can never forge it) and sets `primarySkipped: true` on that `LensResult`. - **Opt-in and back-compatible.** A backend with no declared window is never guard-skipped and never triggers the trim, so every un-annotated review is byte-for-byte unchanged. Window values are operator knowledge about their own deployments — a self-hosted model's served window often differs from the base model's — so faff never writes or infers one. - **An over-window skip carries the same terminal class the 400 already did.** For the case this feature exists to fix the exit class is **unchanged**: an over-window HTTP 400 already mapped to `request-failed` → exit 2, which is already a needs-human class, so the guard simply replaces a 400-derived exit 2 with a guard-derived one at zero network cost. The class shifts in exactly one narrower case: a backend that would otherwise have contributed only an *availability* failure (host down **and** window too small) now contributes a config-fault class instead, so a fully-failed chain containing it surfaces `needs-human` (2) rather than `pass`+skip (5). That is the stricter direction and consistent with the standing no-silent-weakening rule, under which a config fault anywhere in a fully-failed chain surfaces `needs-human`: a window too small for your diffs is actionable operator config, not a transient outage. - **The token estimate is deliberately conservative** (a byte-ratio, no tokenizer): it OVER-estimates so the guard trips early rather than late. It only needs to be approximately right, because the surfacing above is what keeps an imprecise estimate honest in both directions. **Transport families (helper-internal — how `review-call.mjs` dispatches on `provider`; not a recipe to call yourself).
